headline: Two weeks out from the crossing, the taper is visibly underway. Recent easy runs sit low and controlled — the aerobic engine is holding as volume winds down. No running logged in three days; the quiet is deliberate.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is coherent for an athlete winding toward a long self-supported effort. Running volume over the recent four-week window is well up on the prior block, but the last few days have gone quiet — that gap reads as intentional taper, not lost thread, and the four-week base underneath it is substantial. Strength has stayed genuinely consistent through the same stretch, which matters more than usual right now: it's the load that keeps durability alive while running sheds. Steps remain high on training days and drop sharply on rest days, so background time-on-feet is doing real work even on days without a logged run. The one signal to hold loosely is the strain figure reading zero against a healthy tolerance base — that's exactly what a few quiet days produces, and here it describes the taper rather than warning about it.
sections.trends: Zoom out and the shape is a clear build followed by a deliberate wind-down — the recent four-week ramp against the prior block is a big jump, and year-to-date distance sits far ahead of the same point last year. That trajectory makes sense: a long accumulation phase feeding into an event-specific taper. This isn't a plateau or an irregular drift; it's the top of a build being managed down. For a year-round hybrid athlete this is one of the few moments where the training genuinely narrows toward a target, and the underlying base supports doing so without anxiety.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace remains strong from the early-July benchmark, and there's no reason to think it has moved — the recent easy runs holding low HR at comparable paces are indirect confirmation the aerobic ceiling is intact. With the 30-day baseline still accumulating, treat the single threshold figure as a reference point rather than a trend, but nothing in the recent efficiency data contradicts it. For the crossing, threshold isn't the limiter anyway; the sustained low-end aerobic economy on display is the more relevant currency.
sections.zones: The recent runs sit predominantly in Z1–Z2 with only brief touches higher, which is exactly right for a taper feeding a multi-day effort — polarised toward easy, no grey-zone drift. The one exception is the earlier faster session with meaningful Z3 time, but that predates the wind-down and reads as a deliberate quality touch rather than a pattern. Nothing in the recent shape suggests accumulating fatigue from misplaced intensity; the distribution matches the intent of arriving fresh.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions cluster in the low aerobic range with modest peaks, consistent with functional circuit work rather than heavy limit lifting — the HR shape there is stable across the block. The one dropout-affected run sat higher in avg and max than the surrounding chest-strap runs, but that's a single outlier against an otherwise consistent easy-run band, so it doesn't shift the read. Sensor sources broadly agree in what they describe.
sections.calendar: The rhythm through the build was reliably four-modality-rich — running and strength interleaved without long gaps, which is what produced the current base. The recent quiet stretch breaks that cadence, but as a deliberate step-down rather than a lapse. Worth noting the strength cadence has held even as running paused, which keeps the training texture varied rather than collapsing into full rest.
sections.personal_bests: None of the speed PBs are in play during a taper aimed at a multi-day event — the current focus is orthogonal to a fast 5K or 10K. The endurance side is where this block's work compounds, but that's demonstrated over days on the trail rather than in a logged single-run best. Nothing PB-relevant to chase this week.

watch_items: Watch whether the quiet stretch stays a genuine taper or tips into over-rest — a couple of short easy runs before departure would keep the legs primed without adding fatigue.
Watch that easy-run HR stays in its low band whenever running resumes; that remains the cleanest read that fitness is holding through the wind-down.
Watch recovery consistency as pre-event logistics ramp — sleep has been erratic, and a run of poor nights near departure is worth simply being aware of, not acting on.
Watch that strength continues at its current low-intensity cadence rather than escalating close to the event, since it's now the main durability input while running is light.
